newsitem.title: UK: UK spirits industry jubilant after tax cut.
newsitem.headline: UK spirits industry jubilant after tax cut.

text.p: Britain's spirits industry was in jubilant mood after Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke announced another four percent cut in tax duty on spirits from 1800 GMT tonight.
The tax cut will be worth around 26p on a bottle. Clarke cut tax duty on spirits by the same amount last year for the first time since 1895.

"This is just the right move as it will be seen as the UK government providing leadership with a programme of spirits duty cuts in the UK which will send a powerful signal to our world markets where discrimination against Scotch and other spirits continues unabated," said Guinness chairman Tony Greener.
Guinness shares were up 3p at 461. Scotch whisky distiller Glenmorangie was the biggest gainer in the sector, up 10p at 838.
"It's very good news indeed," said Brian Ivory, chief executive of Highland Distilleries in an interview.
"It's good news for Scotland, it's good news for consumers and its good news for the Scotch Whisky industry," he said.
Ivory said he hoped to pass on to consumers the full 25p saving on a bottle of its Famous Grouse blended whisky before Christmas.
Since last year's cut in duty, average prices per bottle of whisky have fallen to 9.85 stg for supermarkets' own label, although the price of brands has risen slightly.

The tax cut will also strengthen the industry's hand in talks with overseas governments like Japan and Taiwan that impose a higher tax on imported Scotch whisky than applied to their home made versions, said Ivory.

"The reducton in the rate on spirits boosts an important industry in the United Kingdom and it also reinforces last year's signal to overseas authorities not to discriminate against our products," said Clarke in his budget statement.
"Only smugglers will regret that we are slowly moving our duty on spirits nearer to the continental (European) level," he added.
